candidate.title: Nextera Mate Pair
candidate.scope: The single Nextera Mate Pair preparation route depicted in the Illumina footer schematic: input DNA, tagmentation with biotinylated junction adapters, circularization, fragmentation, isolation of a biotinylated fragment, adapter ligation, and denaturation/amplification to a product ready for cluster generation. This is a product-preparation outline, without a specified kit revision or a depicted sequencing/data-analysis stage.

states.label: DNA
features: Input DNA is drawn as two parallel blue strands, with dotted continuations at both ends.
The biological target is sequence and physical linkage within the source DNA; no organism or specimen is specified.

evidence.locator: Top: blue double-line substrate labeled 'DNA'

states.label: Biotinylated junction adapter
features: Lime adapter segments bear small biotin symbols and are drawn beneath blue icons labeled 'Transposase'.
These junction adapters are distinct from the P5/P7 adapters depicted at the bottom.

evidence.locator: Top: 'Transposase' and 'Biotinylated junction adapter' labels and associated icons

states.label: Linear DNA fragment with biotinylated junction-adapter ends
features: Two blue DNA strands have lime junction-adapter segments and biotin symbols at their ends.
The preceding image shows adapter insertion sites within the longer DNA; the next downward arrow leads to this released linear fragment.

evidence.locator: Below 'Tagmentation': marked DNA followed by downward arrow to a discrete fragment with lime ends

states.label: Circularized DNA with a biotinylated junction
features: A closed double-line blue circle carries lime adapter segments and biotin symbols at its top.
Circularization brings the two ends of the preceding linear fragment together at this junction.

evidence.locator: Middle left: diagonal arrow from tagged linear fragment to closed circle under 'Circularize'
evidence.rationale: The arrow connects a linear molecule bearing tags at its two ends to a closed molecule with those tags concentrated at one junction; closure therefore associates the formerly separated ends.

states.label: Fragments of the circularized DNA
features: The former circular outline is discontinuous, with a solid blue upper arc containing the lime biotinylated junction and pale separated arcs elsewhere.
This is a fragmentation intermediate, not a second workflow or a pool of separately prepared libraries.

evidence.locator: Middle: rightward arrow labeled 'Fragment' leads from closed circle to discontinuous circular outline

states.label: Isolated biotinylated junction-containing DNA fragment
features: Short linear double-stranded DNA is drawn with an internal lime segment and biotin symbols.
The junction is internal after fragmentation; it is no longer the pair of free ends of the original tagmented fragment.
The flanking blue DNA segments retain the association created by joining the original fragment ends.

evidence.locator: Lower middle: diagonal arrow from fragmented circle to short blue fragment with internal biotinylated junction; 'Isolate biotinylated fragment'

states.label: Forked P5/P7 adapters
features: Two mirrored forked adapter icons flank the isolated DNA fragment.
Their outer arms are labeled P5 and P7; the colors and forked geometry are depicted, but nucleotide sequences and strand end chemistry are not specified.

evidence.locator: Lower left and right: forked adapters flanking selected fragment, with P5 and P7 labels

states.label: Junction-containing DNA with ligated sequencing adapters
features: Boundary state implied by 'Adaptor ligation' before 'Denature and amplify'; no separate ligated-molecule drawing is supplied.
The DNA insert has the selected junction-fragment preparation history and receives the depicted P5/P7 adapter structures.

evidence.locator: Bottom: forked adapter icons, 'Adaptor ligation', then 'Denature and amplify'
evidence.rationale: The explicit ligation caption names adapter attachment; its product is the input to the following combined denaturation/amplification caption, although the intermediate is not separately drawn.

states.label: Product ready for cluster generation
features: Final library is drawn as a linear two-strand product with P5 at the left and P7 at the right.
Its insert derives from the isolated junction-containing fragment.
Internal biotin symbols are not drawn on this final product; persistence of the chemical biotin label through amplification is not established by this depiction.

evidence.locator: Bottom: final horizontal library labeled P5/P7 and 'Product ready for cluster generation'
Route from isolated junction-containing fragment through adapter ligation and amplification
evidence.rationale: The connecting route gives the final insert its junction-fragment origin; the final cartoon alone does not redraw that internal junction.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Fragments the input DNA while adding the depicted biotinylated junction-adapter segments. The marked long-DNA intermediate and the subsequent discrete linear fragment are represented together as this schematic transformation; the output has adapter-bearing biotinylated ends.
operations.mechanism: The figure identifies transposase associated with biotinylated junction adapters and labels the DNA-to-tagged-fragment transformation 'Tagmentation'. No additional enzyme or end-repair chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: Produces a tagged DNA fragment whose two ends can subsequently be joined; this tagging is distinct from installing the final P5/P7 library adapters.

evidence.locator: Top to upper middle: transposase/biotinylated adapter icons, DNA, 'Tagmentation', two downward arrows and tagged fragment

operations.label: Circularize
operations.description: Converts the tagged linear DNA fragment into a closed circular molecule, bringing its two junction-adapter-bearing ends together at the biotinylated junction.
operations.information_effect: The circle physically links the two formerly separated ends of one DNA fragment. This association is the basis for retaining an end-to-end DNA relationship after the rest of the circle is fragmented.

evidence.locator: Center left: linear tagged fragment, diagonal down-left arrow, closed blue circle; 'Circularize'
evidence.rationale: The drawn conversion closes a linear fragment whose tags were at opposite ends; those ends therefore become adjacent at the circular junction. The figure does not name a circularization enzyme.

operations.label: Fragment
operations.description: Breaks the circular DNA into shorter pieces. The drawing retains a solid junction-bearing upper fragment and depicts other portions of the circle as pale discontinuous fragments.
operations.information_effect: Separates the junction-containing region from much of the original DNA fragment; the joined former ends remain together in the junction-bearing piece.

evidence.locator: Middle: closed left circle, horizontal arrow labeled 'Fragment', fragmented right circle with biotinylated upper arc

operations.label: Isolate biotinylated fragment
operations.description: Selects the biotin-bearing junction fragment from the fragmented circle, producing the short linear DNA molecule with an internal biotinylated junction shown below. Other fragmented DNA is not carried along the depicted retained route.
operations.mechanism: Selection is specified by the biotinylated-fragment label; capture chemistry, binding support and attachment state are not depicted.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the material carrying the original fragment-end junction, preserving linked DNA flanks in one short library insert. Biotin selection is a chemical selection; the drawing supplies no measurement of purity or perfect mate-pair specificity.

evidence.locator: Middle right to lower middle: fragmented circle, diagonal downward arrow, 'Isolate biotinylated fragment', and internal-biotin linear product

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Attaches the depicted forked P5/P7 adapters to the isolated linear junction fragment. The adapter-ligated intermediate is implied by the caption before denaturation/amplification.
operations.mechanism: Adapter ligation is explicitly named; no ligase identity or additional preparative reaction is specified.
operations.information_effect: Adds the library interfaces that yield the P5/P7-ended final product while retaining the junction-derived insert.

evidence.locator: Lower panel: P5/P7 forked adapters on both sides of biotinylated DNA fragment; 'Adaptor ligation'

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Processes the adapter-ligated material by the combined depicted denaturation/amplification step to yield the P5/P7 library labeled ready for cluster generation.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert carries the association of the former fragment ends into an amplifiable sequencing library. Inference: paired sequence observations from its two source-DNA flanks could report linkage between those ends rather than sequence continuously through the original long fragment. Sequencing, read orientation and a data product are not depicted.

evidence.locator: Bottom: 'Denature and amplify', downward arrow and P5/P7 final product labeled 'Product ready for cluster generation'
Whole material route: tagged fragment ends are joined in circle, retained in isolated junction fragment, then converted to final library
evidence.rationale: Joining the original fragment ends and retaining both flanks on a selected junction-bearing insert provides an end-linkage carrier for eventual mate-pair sequencing. This deduction establishes neither a read configuration nor a measured linkage result.
